findings.claim: WHITEPAPER.md:271 'every decision was perturbed and had to be caught: 108 flipped allows, 187 flipped denies, all caught'
findings.evidence: The control at scripts/p9_live_simulator_audit.py:511-526 uses `comparator = lambda aws_decision, engine_decision: aws_decision == engine_decision`, then builds `wrong = "allowed" if engine_decision != "allowed" else "implicitDeny"` and requires `not comparator(aws_decision, wrong)`. Because the loop already skipped every disagreeing pair at :518-519, `aws_decision == engine_decision` always holds, and `wrong` is always a different label, so the comparison is always False and the counter always increments. Consequently `flipped_allow_count` is by construction exactly the number of allowed decisions (108) and `flipped_deny_count` exactly the number of denied decisions (187) -- which is what the artifact reports.
findings.assessment: The reported numbers are accurate and the paper reports them faithfully, so this is not an unbacked claim and is not counted in the four gate numbers. But the control cannot fail: it demonstrates that the comparator is not the constant function True, not that a mis-scored decision would have been noticed. The paper's framing ('a zero is worth what the comparator's failure modes are worth') promises more than the code delivers. A reader who recomputes the counts will notice they equal the class sizes exactly.
findings.recommendation: Either strengthen the control (perturb a sampled subset and require the comparator to detect it, recording the sample and the count of detected perturbations) or restate the sentence as 'the comparator was shown not to be vacuous: perturbing any decision changes the verdict, on all 295'. The section-7.1 'why a zero needs a negative control' argument stands either way.
findings.resolution: WHITEPAPER.md:271 no longer says 'all caught'; it now states the control 'perturbs the decision label to a different label, so it cannot fail by construction: it confirms the comparator distinguishes the three decision classes, not that the engine is right'. Matches scripts/p9_live_simulator_audit.py:513-526.
